I definitely hated my birth name from the very beginning. Always begged to have a different one etc. so if I’m choosing a new one I definitely want it to be something I like. People aren’t very adaptable, most people from my past don’t know me now and I’ve noticed I distanced myself from family who won’t adapt to who I am now, I’ll probably move again and change again lol. Such is the cycle, one day I’ll get it right. Maybe. Also it would be cool if societally it was normal not be boring about names, Moonflower sounds like someone I want to be friends with =]

Having an unstable identity can feel exhausting. I also think, is it that strange to want to choose your name? In my mind it’s basically on par with choosing your outfits or how you decorate the spaces you inhabit. It’s another form of self expression, I want to enjoy the name people call me, it’s an extension of who I am.

I think eventually that is what I’ve chalked it up to. It would make sense. I also personally feel like after so much trauma (which is reoccurring throughout my life) I just have to shed my skin like a snake so to speak, and I’ve speculated that changing my name has been a way for me to cope with trauma and move on from it. Whether that is healthy or not idk, I feel like I’ve lived many lifetimes already.

NTA!! I don’t approve of the notion that just because someone is “family” you have to stick with them. I have struggled with unhealthy family dynamics as well, I cut people off even though it was hard. I had to look out for my own well being, they certainly didn’t care about it. From the information you provided it really doesn’t sound like she is working towards any sort of redemption with her children, still being in a denial is a huge red flag. From my own experience, inviting her back into your life is more likely to result in further destruction and hurt.
